Happy Tuesday! Furlenco is heading to Dalal Street for a potential Rs 1,200 crore IPO. This and more in today’s ETtech Morning Dispatch.

Also in the letter:

■ Microsoft’s new India hub

■ Ashwini Vaishnaw on AI safety

■ Indian diaspora founders catch unicorns

Furniture rental company Furlenco gears up for Rs 1,200-crore IPO

Ajith Mohan Karimpana, founder, Furlenco

Subscription-based furniture company Furlenco, backed by the makers of Kurlon and Sleepwell mattresses,

is planning a potential Rs 1,000-1,200 crore initial public offering (IPO), sources said.

IPO details:

Furlenco is seeking a valuation of around Rs 7,000 crore, sources cited above said. The final valuation will be decided closer to the IPO depending on market conditions and the response during investor roadshows, they added.

The IPO is expected to be launched in the next fiscal year.

The Bengaluru-based company is expected to soon finalise ICICI Securities as an advisor.

Financials: Founded in 2012, Furlenco reported Rs 370 crore in revenue from operations in FY26, up 62% year-on-year. Its net profit jumped 19-fold to Rs 59.5 crore during the year, while Ebitda (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization) nearly doubled to Rs 129.5 crore, translating into an Ebitda margin of 35%.

Snapdeal parent AceVector files red herring prospectus; cuts IPO size

Rohit Bansal (left) and Kunal Bahl, cofounders of Snapdeal and Unicommerce parent AceVector Group

Snapdeal and Unicommerce parent AceVector

has slashed its IPO size , according to its red herring prospectus filed on Monday.

Details:

The size of its offer-for-sale component is also being reduced by 35%.

Investors including SoftBank, Nexus Venture Partners, Foxconn and others will trim their stake.

Founders Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal, who together hold around a 34% stake directly and through other related entities, are not selling any stake.

AceVector now plans to raise Rs 287 crore in fresh capital against Rs 300 crore earlier.

The price band is expected to be announced on September 22.

Financials: During fiscal 2026, AceVector's operating revenue grew 30% to Rs 510 crore, even as it cut down its net loss to a third at Rs 45 crore against Rs 126 crore in FY25.

Moneyview eyes $600 million IPO valuation, 20% below its last private market peg

Sanjay Aggarwal and Puneet Agarwal, cofounders, Moneyview

Digital lending platform Moneyview is

seeking a valuation of Rs 5,985 crore ($600 million) at the upper end of the price band for its IPO (initial public offering), which is about 20% lower than the roughly Rs 7,500-crore valuation at which it last raised primary capital in December 2022.

IPO details: The company has set a price band of Rs 32-34 per share for the IPO, which will open for subscription on September 24 and close on September 28.

The deal: Existing shareholders, including Accel, Tiger Global, and Ribbit Capital, along with promoters Puneet Agarwal and Sanjay Aggarwal, are selling shares in the OFS component of the IPO.

Investor gains: Venture capital firms Accel, Ribbit Capital, and Tiger Global are sitting on multi-fold returns on their investments in digital lender Moneyview at the upper end of its IPO price band, despite the public issue valuation being below its last primary funding round.

Microsoft in ‘action cycle’ on data centres, says India president Puneet Chandok

Puneet Chandok, President, Microsoft India and South Asia

Microsoft

is continuously scouting for new data centre regions in India and other markets as demand for cloud and AI infrastructure grows, said Puneet Chandok, the company’s president for India and South Asia.

Verbatim: “We’re always looking at it because, as you can imagine, these regions take a lot of time to build,” Chandok told us. “The reason we’re first out of the gates, the reason we’re not in an intent cycle but in an action cycle, unlike the industry today where people are announcing everything, is we started a long time ago,” he said.

New launch: On Monday, Microsoft announced its fourth cloud region in Hyderabad, positioned as a strategic hub for Asia and the Global South. Its other Indian cloud regions are in Pune, Chennai and Mumbai.

Chandok said India currently has about 2 GW of data centre capacity but will need 10-14 GW in the coming years. Globally, Microsoft is expanding from around 12 GW today to more than 38 GW by 2032, with India expected to remain a “meaningful part” of that growth, he said.

On AI safety: On AI safety, Chandok reiterated Microsoft’s stance that “AI has to be built in the service of humanity” and that AI systems and agents must remain under human control.

Other Top Stories By Our Reporters

Ashwini Vaishnaw, Union minister for IT

Ashwini Vaishnaw on AI safety: Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that regulating AI will take both law and technical safeguards, and that companies building the technology must take the lead on safety.

Indian diaspora founders’ unicorn value: Founders who grew up in India have built or cofounded 205 current and former unicorns overseas, with about $560 billion of the companies’ value attributed to them, according to a report by Prosus and Dealroom.

SOURCE 2: The Hindu - Editorials

### Presumed ineligible: On the Election Commission of India’s SIR process
22 Sep 2026 | https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editorial/presumed-ineligible-on-the-election-commission-of-indias-sir-process/article71491681.ece

Not one eligible elector should be left out of the electoral rolls. This statement appears in nearly every document released by the Election Commission of India (ECI) as part of the ongoing SIR process , and the Supreme Court of India, which is hearing petitions challenging the SIR, has also used this refrain. Yet, according to an ECI counter-affidavit filed in the Court, by early September 2026, out of more than 38 lakh appeals submitted to SIR appellate tribunals in West Bengal, just over 1,22,000 appeals were disposed of (a disposal rate of just 3.2%) and 1,13,943 electors were added back to the rolls (an inclusion rate of nearly 93%). This suggests that the claims/corrections phase in the West Bengal SIR — during which judicial officers deployed for verification deemed 27 lakh of the 60 lakh electors flagged for “logical discrepancies” to be ineligible — was deeply flawed. More than 22 lakh of those found ineligible have since appealed, and ECI data show that more than nine in 10 cases decided by the tribunals have ended with the electors back on the rolls. If these “inclusion” and “disposal” rates hold, the majority of the 27 lakh electors should not have been ineligible in the first place and are now struggling to get back on the rolls — an indication that massive disenfranchisement preceded the West Bengal Assembly polls. With municipal elections in the State approaching, the ECI must speed up the appellate process and restore eligible electors to the rolls.

In Phase 3 of the SIR, The Hindu ’s analysis found that in 24 out of Delhi’s 70 constituencies, the draft roll now records fewer electors than those who voted in the February 2025 Assembly election. Such large-scale deletion cannot hold unless there was a major migration process in the capital region or large numbers of voters were never ordinarily resident in Delhi. A more plausible answer is that the enumeration itself has struck off actual voters. The process puts the onus of proving eligibility on the elector, and the ECI’s dropping of enumeration forms at homes has not translated into full enumeration. Requiring electors to link themselves to rolls drawn in the early 2000s then manufactures “discrepancies” even when documents are valid. In Delhi, this “mapping” has put 13.79 lakh electors under notice with a further 19.33 lakh flagged for “logical discrepancies” on undefined grounds. While hearing the Bihar SIR petitions, the Court had intervened sharply to stop eligible voters from being struck off. Its permissiveness in the year since, towards an insouciant ECI has allowed disenfranchisement on a scale that will remain a black mark on the jurisprudence of universal adult franchise in India. As the Court hears petitions on Delhi and West Bengal, it must compel the ECI to reverse course.

Published - September 22, 2026 12:20 am IST
